meta.preheader: NIFTY 50 rose 0.58% to 25,291.10 as FMCG and bank shares gained; foreign investors bought ₹4,865 crore (provisional); the rupee closed 27 paise stronger at 93.92.
meta.subject: Kubeerra Market Brief · Tue 17 Nov: NIFTY 50 ends 0.58% higher at 25,291.10; Nasdaq falls 2.49% overnight

brief: The NIFTY 50 rose 0.58% to 25,291.10 and the Sensex 0.63% to 82,104.79 on Monday, led by FMCG and bank shares, while the NIFTY Smallcap 100 fell 1.10% and declines outnumbered advances about two to one on NSE (Upstox News).
Foreign investors bought a net ₹4,865 crore and domestic institutions sold ₹3,519 crore (provisional, Kotak Neo). The rupee closed 27 paise stronger at 93.92 per dollar (PTI).
October wholesale price inflation rose to 12.29% from 11.39%, with fuel and power at 32.84% (Upstox News). Brent settled 3.55% lower at $92.44 a barrel (Newsquawk).

Overseas, the Nasdaq fell 2.49%, the S&P 500 1.92% and the Dow 1.41% as chip shares declined ahead of Nvidia's results; the dollar index rose to 103.50, its highest since April 2025 (Eurasia Business News, Reuters).
IBJA gold fell ₹838 to ₹1,34,971 per 10 g and silver ₹7,749 to ₹1,70,251 per kg on Monday (IBJA).

outlook.headline: Wholesale inflation above 12%, crude near $92 and US yields above 5% frame the week before Nvidia's results

drivers.title: Inflation and the RBI
drivers.text: October wholesale price inflation rose to 12.29% from 11.39%, with fuel and power at 32.84% (Upstox News). Barclays expects a 25 basis point repo rate rise on 4 December and another in February, to 6%; economists at Emkay Global and IDFC First Bank also expect rises at both meetings, from a repo rate of 5.50% (Business Standard). Rate expectations reach bond yields, deposit rates and loan rates.

drivers.title: Crude oil
drivers.text: Brent's January contract settled 3.55% lower at $92.44 a barrel on Monday. Bloomberg cited ample physical supply, with the IEA expecting a surplus of about 2 million barrels a day this quarter, even as attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz continued (Rigzone). India imports most of its crude, so oil prices reach the import bill, the rupee and fuel inflation.

drivers.title: Foreign flows and the rupee
drivers.text: Exchange data show foreign investors bought a net ₹84,167 crore of Indian shares from 1 to 16 November (provisional, Kotak Neo). HDFC Sky, citing NSDL data, said November's buying so far, about $8.9 billion, is already the largest for any month on record, and linked it partly to worries about AI-linked trades overseas. PTI said the inflows helped the rupee gain 27 paise on Monday.

global_cues.title: US technology shares
global_cues.text: On Monday the Nasdaq fell 2.49% and the S&P 500 1.92% as Nvidia, down 4.12%, led another fall in chip shares before its results (Eurasia Business News, AP). Global technology sentiment reaches Indian IT shares and foreign investors' allocation between markets.

global_cues.title: US yields and the dollar
global_cues.text: The US 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 5.12%, while the dollar index rose 0.1% to 103.50, its highest since April 2025; Reuters reported futures pricing a 93.4% chance of a 25 basis point Fed rise on 9 December (CME FedWatch). US yields and the dollar reach India through the rupee and foreign flows into emerging markets.

global_cues.title: Asian markets
global_cues.text: On Monday Japan's Nikkei fell 2.42% and Korea's Kospi 3.59%, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose 0.49% (HDFC Sky, AP). Asian moves shape the regional mood at India's open.

us.title: The session
us.text: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell for a third session, led by technology, as reports of leadership changes at Nvidia continued before its results; Nvidia closed 4.12% lower at $156.14 (Eurasia Business News).

us.title: Chips and banks
us.text: Chip stocks also fell after the Commerce Department announced limits on Chinese customers' remote access to advanced US chips (Eurasia Business News). Technology was the weakest sector, down 2.98%, and bank shares came under pressure after reports of online service outages at several large US banks (Newsquawk).

us.title: Data and rates
us.text: The New York Fed's Empire State manufacturing index fell to 7.8, against 16.7 expected (Stock Titan). The 10-year Treasury yield eased about 2 basis points to 5.117% (Newsquawk).

events.title: Markets price a December Fed rise
events.text: Fed funds futures implied a 93.4% chance of a 25 basis point rise at the meeting ending 9 December (CME FedWatch, reported by Reuters). Vice Chair Jefferson called inflation the key concern, and Cleveland Fed President Hammack favoured smaller, step-by-step rises (Newsquawk). The channel to India: the dollar, the rupee and foreign flows.

events.title: US curbs on remote chip access
events.text: The Commerce Department announced limits on Chinese companies' remote access to advanced US chips through overseas data centres (Eurasia Business News), and chip shares in Asia fell too, with SK hynix down 7.9% (AP). The channel to India: global technology sentiment and foreign flows into emerging markets.

commentary.text: Spot gold fell as low as $3,830 an ounce on Monday, its lowest since October 2025, with the dollar near its strongest since April 2025 (Reuters).
Zaner Metals' Peter Grant said inflation data had lifted expectations of a Fed rise, and with them yields and the dollar, which weigh on gold (Reuters).

Silver fell more than gold; independent analyst Nikos Tzabouras cited high rates, a strong dollar and AI-related worries (Reuters). USAGOLD noted the Silver Institute's projection of a sixth straight annual silver market deficit in 2026.

stories.headline: India's October goods trade deficit widened to $39.88 billion as gold imports rose
stories.what: The deficit was the widest in a year, up from $30.21 billion in September and above the $32.25 billion a Reuters poll had expected. Exports were $49.47 billion and imports $89.35 billion; gold imports rose to $5.51 billion from $1.8 billion (Reuters, released Fri 13 Nov).
stories.why: A wider goods deficit means more demand for dollars to pay for imports, which reaches markets through the rupee and the current account.

stories.headline: SEBI set up a group led by NSE's chief to review the rules for IPOs and other share issues
stories.what: On 16 Nov SEBI formed a sub-group of its Primary Market Advisory Committee, headed by NSE's Ashishkumar Chauhan, to review rules on eligibility for IPOs, QIPs and preferential issues, promoter lock-in, pricing, allotment and disclosures. Its recommendations go to the committee first; no rule has changed (Kotak Neo, PSU Watch).
stories.why: These rules govern how companies raise capital and what investors are told in offer documents.

link.name: Kubeerra guide: What is a mutual fund?

category_explainer.text: Under SEBI's categorisation circular of 26 February 2026, a liquid fund is an open-ended debt scheme that invests only in debt and money market securities maturing in up to 91 days; AMFI notes these include treasury bills, commercial paper and certificates of deposit. AMFI adds that liquid funds aim to hold well-rated paper, so the possibility of a default is very low, though not nil. Each scheme's riskometer level is set out in the fund house's own documents.

learn.title: How a fund's assets can fall while money keeps coming in
paragraphs: A mutual fund category's assets change for two reasons: net flows (money invested minus money withdrawn) and the change in the market value of what the schemes hold, known as mark-to-market or MTM.
In October, equity funds took net inflows of ₹32,994 crore, yet equity fund assets fell 1.1% to ₹37.15 lakh crore, which AMFI attributed to MTM losses (AMFI Monthly Note, October 2026).
So a rise or fall in a category's assets does not by itself show whether investors added or withdrew money; AMFI's monthly flow figures show that separately.
